newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 49.54 points, closing at 7722.33.
* Montgomery Ward & Co Inc, facing a financial pinch, has stopped paying many of its vendors, sources said.
* The Federal Trade Commission said it would not move to block Boeing's plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas.
* Market Place: Analysts are calling certain front-office applications, such as sales force automation and customer support programs, the fastest-growing segment of the software industry.
* U.S. officials contend that China improperly diverted an American supercomputer to one of its military research facilities earlier this year.
* EMI Group acquired a 50 percent stake in the publishing company from Berry Gordy Jr. for $132 million.
* Motorola Inc plans to take a $170 million pre-tax charge against second-quarter earnings to phase out its limited participation in the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market.
* The New York New Media Association has attracted about 30 private investors seeking to put their money into high-technology start-ups in return for stakes in the companies.
* The California Supreme Court has ruled that Kaiser Permanente manipulated an arbitration system under which patients can file malpractice claims.
* The dollar rose against the German mark amid support for the strength of the U.S. currency.
* Soybean prices dropped, reflecting expectations that farmers would bring in a record crop.
* Chrysler Corp reported a drop in sales for June of 4 percent.
* Further evidence has arrived that the U.S. economy was slowing.

* Sears, Roebuck and Co's store in East Los Angeles has transformed itself into a mecca for largely Hispanic customers by bringing in merchandise catering to the community, such as soccer shirts featuring Latin American teams.
* Troubles at Viacom's Blockbuster continue, with the video store unit seeing earnings far below analyst expectations, forcing its parent company to take a $300 million write-down.
